socfpga_smmu.h

SMMU hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Address Translation Mappings

Text: SDM VA to PA Translation Address Space: 512 MB | Granule: 4 KB

Virtual Address (29 bits total)

Bits  0-11  |  Granule Offset|  --> Ignored (4 KB pages)
Bits 12-20  |  L1 Index (9b) |  --> 512 entries
Bits 21-28  |  L0 Index (8b) |  --> 256 entries
Flow

+----------+  +----------+  +-------------------+

 L0     |----->|   L1     |----->| Physical Address  |
Table   |      |  Table   |      |                   |

+----------+  +----------+  +-------------------+

Text: Peripheral VA to PA Translation Address Space: 1 TB | Granule: 4 KB

Virtual Address (40 bits total)

Bits  0-11  | Granule Offset |  --> Ignored (4 KB pages)
Bits 12-20  |  2 MB Offset   |  --> Ignored (using 2 MB blocks)
Bits 21-29  |  L2 Index (9b) |  --> 512 entries
Bits 30-38  |  L1 Index (9b) |  --> 512 entries
Bit   39    |  L0 Index (1b) |  --> 2 entries
Flow

+----------+  +----------+  +----------+  +-------------------+

 L0     |----->|   L1     |----->|   L2     |----->|  Physical Address |
Table   |      |  Table   |      |  Table   |      |                   |

+----------+  +----------+  +----------+  +-------------------+

L0 Table (2 entries): [0]  0x0000_0000_00 to 0x7FFF_FFFF_FF (in use) [1]  0x8000_0000_00 to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FF (unused)

L1 Example Mappings

[0]  device_mem [1]  device_mem [2]  normal_mem [3]  device_mem

Summary

  • 3-level page table walk

  • L0: 2 entries, L1: 512 entries, L2: 512 entries

  • 2 MB block mappings (21 LSBs ignored)

Constants
SMMU stream IDs

Stream IDs for SoC peripherals. smmu_enable programs one stream-table entry for each ID from 1 through the maximum.

SMMU_MAX_STREAM_ID

Highest stream ID.

SMMU_STREAM_ID_NAND

Stream ID for NAND.

SMMU_STREAM_ID_SDMMC

Stream ID for SDMMC.

SMMU_STREAM_ID_DMA0

Stream ID for DMA 0.

SMMU_STREAM_ID_DMA1

Stream ID for DMA 1.

SMMU_STREAM_ID_SDM

Stream ID for the SDM.

context_desc_t

Represents an ARM SMMUv3 Context Descriptor (CD).

This heavily packed, 64-byte aligned structure defines the Stage 1 memory translation regime for a specific peripheral or execution context. It configures the Translation Table Base Addresses (TTB0/TTB1), ASID, Translation Granules (TG0/TG1), memory attributes (MAIR), and fault handling behaviors.

stream_table_t

Represents an ARM SMMUv3 Stream Table Entry (STE).

This 64-byte structure acts as the root of the configuration hierarchy for an incoming hardware transaction. Based on the incoming Stream ID, the SMMU looks up this STE to determine if the transaction should bypass translation, generate an abort, or proceed with Stage 1/Stage 2 translation. If Stage 1 is configured, the S1ContextPtr field points to the corresponding context_desc_t.

command_desc_t

Represents an ARM SMMUv3 Command Queue entry.

The SMMU Command Queue is a circular buffer residing in memory, used by software to issue instructions directly to the SMMU hardware. Each command is exactly 16 bytes (four 32-bit words). Typical commands include TLB invalidations (CMD_TLBI) and synchronization requests (CMD_SYNC).

smmu_descriptors_t

A master aggregation structure containing all in-memory tables required by the SMMUv3 controller.

This massive structure holds the linear Stream Table, Context Descriptors, the Command Queue, Event Queue, and the fully populated multi-level translation page tables for both the 512MB (SDM) and 1TB (Peripheral) virtual address spaces.  By defining this as a single struct, the driver ensures all required alignment boundaries (e.g., 4KB page bounds, 64-byte cache lines) are strictly honored by the linker during bare-metal instantiation.

smmu_enable
int32_t smmu_enable(
void
)

Bootstraps and enables the SMMUv3 hardware controller.

This routine writes the base addresses of the pre-allocated Stream Table and Command Queue into the SMMU's memory-mapped registers (SMMU_STRTAB_BASE, SMMU_CMDQ_BASE). It configures the queue pointers (PROD/CONS) and finally sets the SMMU_CR0.SMMUEN bit to activate memory translation and protection on the bus.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code if the hardware fails to respond or validate the table pointers.

smmu_disable
int32_t smmu_disable(
void
)

Safely halts the SMMUv3 controller.

This function initiates an orderly teardown by draining any pending DMA transactions, pushing a CMD_SYNC into the command queue, and clearing the SMMU_CR0.SMMUEN bit to return the bus to a bypass/passthrough state.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code if the hardware hangs during sync.

smmu_deinit
int32_t smmu_deinit(
void
)

Tears down the software context for the SMMU driver. This releases any allocated descriptors and resets the driver's internal tracking state, allowing the module to be safely reinitialized later if needed.

Returns

0 on success.
